claims.text: The nanoparticles are initially solid, overall-equiatomic Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu high-entropy alloys.
These initially solid nanoparticles contain inherent local compositional fluctuations despite their overall equiatomic composition.
Local compositional fluctuations create atomic-scale soft spots with depressed local melting temperatures.
The soft spots trigger earlier and more spatially nonuniform premelting than occurs in uniformly composed nanoparticles.
The proposed test uses in situ high-temperature ramping with high-resolution TEM, nanoscale calorimetry, and elemental mapping under an inert atmosphere.
Particle size, shape, and heating rate are to be held constant during comparison.
Local compositional heterogeneities produce zones with reduced barriers to melting.
The constituent elements have different melting points.
Limited atomic mobility can persist under the relevant nonequilibrium processing conditions.
Slight local deviations from nominal composition require less thermal energy to become liquid.
Compositionally soft regions nucleate liquid before the surrounding matrix.
Early liquid nucleation at soft regions governs the overall premelting and melting response.
Premelting will initiate at discrete locations that coincide with measurable compositional fluctuations.
Uniformly composed baseline nanoparticles will melt more homogeneously and at a higher, more uniform temperature.
Single-metal or uniformly alloyed baseline particles lacking local compositional fluctuations will melt simultaneously without early nucleation at discrete sites.
The mechanism applies while the nanoparticle remains a solid solution and diffusion is too slow to homogenize its local fluctuations.
The mechanism is limited to rapid heating and processing histories that do not erase compositional heterogeneity.

Failure to observe preferential liquid nucleation at compositionally fluctuating sites, together with behavior indistinguishable from the uniform baseline, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The experiment is described as gradual heating through the premelting and melting regimes, whereas the stated applicability boundary restricts the hypothesis to rapid heating; no ramp-rate criterion reconciles these descriptions.
